title: pricing & packaging back-of-envelope notes
content:
Goal: quick, shareable assumptions for hosted API token pricing + committed/dedicated packaging. Super rough - for internal discussion.

ASSUMPTIONS (very rough)
- Baseline hardware & infra: amortized inference cost (including infra, storage, monitoring, SRE ops) per 1M tokens: $2.00 on average for mid-sized open models with quantization/batching. (=> $0.000002 per token) - this is conservative for optimized runtime; on larger/long-context models cost could be ~2-5x.
- Avg request size: 60 input tokens + 60 output tokens = 120 tokens per call. (Varies a lot by use-case.)
- QPS/batching: effective batch/caching discounts reduce per-token infra cost by ~30% at steady state for chat-heavy workloads.
- Margin target on hosted API: 60-70% gross margin after infra & ops.

SIMPLE TOKEN MATH (hosted)
- Cost assumptions: infra cost per 1M tokens = $2.00 -> per token = $0.000002. Add model licensing & SLO ops overhead say $0.000003 => total unit cost = $0.000005/token.
- Target price to customer (80% gross margin): price_per_token = unit_cost / (1 - margin) = 0.000005 / 0.2 = $0.000025/token -> $0.025 per 1k tokens.
- Round to market-friendly numbers: $0.02- $0.03 per 1k tokens for standard open model endpoints.

Tier sketch (hosted API)
- Free: 500k tokens / month (intro)
- Starter: $20/mo = 800k tokens @ $0.025k -> gives 800k tokens bundled (good for small dev/prototype)
- Team: $150/mo = 6M tokens (discounted bulk)
- Growth: $1,200/mo = 60M tokens (effective price ~ $0.02 per 1k)
- Scale: custom + committed discounts or negotiated SLOs + premium support
Notes: pricing should reflect per-token but we also do per-request limits, concurrency, and network egress caps. Bundled tokens & rate limits reduce surprise bills.

Dedicated / Reserved capacity thought exercise
- For Dedicated customers we price on two axes: reserved baseline (monthly commit) + usage overage at discounted hosted rate.
- Example: 4x A100-equivalent GPU pool serving model family X. Monthly infra cost (amortized + infra ops + networking) = $40k. Target margin 40% (since enterprise support & SLA). => list price ~ $67k/mo. Offer 20% discount for 12mo commit = $53.6k/mo.
- Translate into effective per-token: if customer uses 2B tokens/mo on that pool -> $53.6k / 2B = $0.0000268/token (~$0.0268 per 1k). But dedicated customers typically value predictability & isolation more than pure unit price.

Embeddings pricing idea
- Embeddings are cheaper per unit but have long tails (indexing costs, storage). Base pricing: $0.005 per 1k tokens for create? Hmm better: charge per embedding vector: $0.0004 / embed (assuming 1 embed per 1k tokens average). Provide storage & similarity search add-ons (per GB/month).

Discounting / quantization / model-class buckets
- Put models into pricing buckets: small (chatty, short context), medium (longer contexts), large (LLAMA2-70B style). Each bucket has recommended price multiplier: small x1, medium x2.5, large x6. Quantization / faster kernels recommended for cheaper tiers.
- Offer "fast-path" low-latency tier at +30% price.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need more accurate unit-costs from infra (SRE/infra team) per model & per-region breakdown (US vs EU). Ticketed: PRJ-789.
- How to bake in caching savings (prefix caching) into published prices vs deliver as "Optimize" recommendations?
- Embeddings: nail down vector storage costs + common embed dims we want to support.
- Consider a developer-friendly metric: price per 1k tokens for generation + separate price per 1k tokens for embeddings. Keep numbers round (0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05).

Notes to self: share with Priya + Noah; align on basic published numbers before next growth planning sync. Mark this as working doc - will iterate with real infra numbers and legal on SLA/enterprise terms.

References / related artifacts: CON-3456 (pricing model RFC), PRJ-789 (dedicated pricing calc), github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs#42

End of quick notes.
